marks.gloss_en: if two witnesses can bring a man to the severe death penalty, shall they not bring him to the light korban?
אמרו לו: מה אם ירצה לומר מזיד הייתי יפטר -- the korban hinges on his own account, so witnesses cannot impose it; binds the Chachamim, not R' Meir
the Chachamim exempt him from the korban
if the mouth, which does not obligate money (read: a fine), obligates an oath, witnesses, who do obligate money, surely obligate an oath
the mouth does not obligate money?! הודאת בעל דין כמאה עדים דמי
a litigant's own admission is as a hundred witnesses (for money, though not for a fine)
מאי ממון — קנס: read 'money' as a fine, which one's own admission never imposes
the mouth is stronger: it obligates a korban, which witnesses (per the Chachamim) do not; the אשם reformulation (3b.10) is dismissed as the same ground -- אשם היינו קרבן
רבי חייא כרבי מאיר סבירא ליה -- for R' Chiyya, who follows R' Meir, witnesses DO obligate a korban (kv_edim_korban), so the asymmetry vanishes inside his framework
the mouth obligates the added fifth, which witnesses do not
as R' Chiyya (with R' Meir) derives the korban by kal vachomer, so the fifth -- inside his framework the asymmetry vanishes
the mouth is subject to neither contradiction nor hazama; witnesses are subject to both -- UNANSWERED: the admission-source falls (אלא אתיא מעד אחד)
if a single witness, who does not obligate money, obligates an oath, two witnesses, who obligate money, surely obligate an oath
a single witness's oath is on the very matter he attests; the oath sought here is on what the witnesses did NOT address -- unanswered
the partial admitter is really dodging until he can pay, so the Torah lays an oath on him to force full admission -- a psychology absent when witnesses attest, hence the need for the kal vachomer
two witnesses say 'you ate forbidden fat' and he denies it: R' Meir obligates the korban
